Beginner.theme: Week 1 — Web Architecture & Semantic HTML5
Beginner.goal: Master how the web works, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, browser rendering, semantic elements, accessible forms, and SEO metadata.

resources.title: MDN Web Docs: How the Internet Works
MDN Web Docs: Getting Started with HTML5

dailyBreakdown.task: Study client-server communication, DNS lookup flow, and HTTP request-response cycles
Learn semantic HTML5 landmarks: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <section>, <footer>
Implement accessible web forms with semantic inputs, labels, pattern regex, and client validation
Audit web pages for accessibility using Chrome Lighthouse and screen reader navigation
Project Lab: Build an accessible semantic product landing page conforming to W3C standards

Beginner.milestone: Build an accessible, responsive semantic landing page and achieve a 100/100 Lighthouse accessibility score.

Beginner.theme: Week 2 — CSS3 Layouts, Flexbox & CSS Grid
Beginner.goal: Master the CSS box model, modern layout engines (Flexbox & CSS Grid), responsive design, and CSS custom properties.

resources.title: CSS-Tricks: A Complete Guide to Flexbox
CSS-Tricks: A Complete Guide to CSS Grid

dailyBreakdown.task: Master the CSS Box Model: content, padding, border, margin, and box-sizing: border-box
Practice Flexbox: flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, flex-wrap, and flex-grow
Build complex responsive dashboards using CSS Grid template areas and auto-fit/minmax
Implement fluid typography and responsive breakpoints using mobile-first media queries
Project Lab: Build a fully responsive multi-device product catalog with card grids and navbar

Beginner.milestone: Create a modern responsive eCommerce dashboard layout that adapts seamlessly across mobile, tablet, and desktop.

Beginner.theme: Week 3 — Core JavaScript Foundations & DOM Manipulation
Beginner.goal: Understand JavaScript syntax, primitive types, functions, scope, arrays, objects, and dynamic DOM manipulation.

resources.title: freeCodeCamp: JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures

dailyBreakdown.task: Study variables (let, const), primitives, truthy/falsy evaluation, and strict equality (===)
Practice arrow functions, default parameters, function expressions, and lexical scope
Master higher-order array methods: map(), filter(), reduce(), find(), and some()
Learn DOM query methods (querySelector), attribute mutation, and event delegation
Project Lab: Build an interactive Kanban task board with add, edit, filter, and delete functionality

Beginner.milestone: Build an interactive Task Management application with dynamic DOM rendering and persistent localStorage.

Beginner.theme: Week 4 — Asynchronous JavaScript & REST API Integration
Beginner.goal: Master asynchronous execution, the event loop, Promises, Async/Await, and handling REST APIs with Fetch.

resources.title: MDN Web Docs: Working with the Fetch API

dailyBreakdown.task: Understand the JS Event Loop, microtask queue (Promises), and macrotask queue (setTimeout)
Create and consume Promises with .then(), .catch(), and .finally()
Refactor asynchronous workflows to async/await syntax with robust try/catch blocks
Make GET, POST, PUT, DELETE requests using the Fetch API with custom headers and error handling
Project Lab: Build a live Weather & Forecast Web App fetching data from an external REST API

Beginner.milestone: Deliver a live Weather Dashboard displaying real-time forecasts with loading skeletons and error fallbacks.

Beginner.theme: Week 5 — Version Control, Git & Modern Tooling
Beginner.goal: Master Git version control, GitHub collaboration workflows, package managers (npm/pnpm), and build tools like Vite.

resources.title: Pro Git Book (Free by Scott Chacon)
GitHub Guides: Understanding the GitHub Flow

dailyBreakdown.task: Learn git init, staging with git add, committing with semantic messages, and viewing git log
Practice feature branching: git checkout -b, git merge, and resolving manual merge conflicts
Configure GitHub remotes, push code, open pull requests, and perform structured code reviews
Explore npm: package.json, dependencies vs devDependencies, and semantic versioning (^ vs ~)
Project Lab: Scaffold a production-grade Vanilla TypeScript project using Vite and deploy to GitHub Pages

Beginner.milestone: Establish a structured GitHub repository with protected branches, pull request workflow, and automated deployment.

Beginner.theme: Week 6 — React.js Fundamentals & Component Architecture
Beginner.goal: Understand React declarative UI, JSX syntax, functional components, props, state management with useState, and effects.

dailyBreakdown.task: Learn how React reconciliation works, Virtual DOM diffing, and writing valid JSX syntax
Build modular, reusable components and pass data and callbacks via props
Manage component state with useState; understand state immutability and updater functions
Control side effects with useEffect: dependency arrays, API data fetching, and cleanup functions
Project Lab: Build a React Crypto Tracker with live price search, filtering, and watchlists

Beginner.milestone: Build a functional single-page React cryptocurrency dashboard with live search, sorting, and state persistence.

Beginner.theme: Week 7 — Advanced React, Context API & Client Routing
Beginner.goal: Scale React applications with custom hooks, global state management via Context API, and client-side routing.

resources.title: React.dev: Passing Data Deeply with Context
React.dev: Reusing Logic with Custom Hooks

dailyBreakdown.task: Create custom hooks (useFetch, useLocalStorage, useWindowSize) for reusable business logic
Implement React Context API with useReducer for scalable global application state
Configure React Router: BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, dynamic params (:id), and ProtectedRoutes
Optimize renders with React.memo, useMemo for heavy calculations, and useCallback for handlers
Project Lab: Build a complete Multi-Page eCommerce Store with cart context and checkout flow

Beginner.milestone: Develop an eCommerce application with multi-route navigation, global cart context, and custom checkout hooks.

Beginner.theme: Week 8 — Testing, Web Performance & Production Deployment
Beginner.goal: Ensure application reliability with automated unit testing (Vitest/React Testing Library) and deploy to production.

resources.title: Testing Library: React Testing Library Tutorial

dailyBreakdown.task: Write unit tests for UI components using Vitest and React Testing Library (render, screen, fireEvent)
Implement code-splitting and dynamic route imports with React.lazy and Suspense
Audit performance: optimize asset sizes, font rendering, LCP (Largest Contentful Paint), and CLS
Set up automated GitHub Actions workflow to run linter and tests on pull requests
Capstone: Deploy full-stack frontend application to Vercel/Netlify with custom domain and HTTPS

Beginner.milestone: Pass all automated unit tests and successfully deploy a production-grade React web app with automated CI/CD.
